locator.section: Chapter 8, Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation -- hydrogen rearrangements; introduced as 'An unusual example of a triple-H rearrangement is shown in Equation 8.80 (Abbott et al. 1979).'

evidence.curator_note: DRAWN FIGURE: a single straight reaction arrow labelled 'r3H' from 2-methoxy-4-methyl-1,3,2-dioxaphospholane 2-oxide with '+.' printed on the phosphoryl oxygen (five-membered ring O-CH(CH3)-CH2-O-P; P also carries =O+. and OCH3) to 'C3H3.' plus a phosphorus ion drawn as +OH double-bonded to P with HO, HO and OCH3 as the other three substituents. Book draws 0 arc(s) -- there is not a single curved arrow or fishhook anywhere in Equation 8.80 -- so ALL FIVE encoded moves are curator-supplied, and both the electron routing and the C3H3 isomer are curator choices, not book statements. CURATOR CHOICES, stated explicitly: (a) each of the three ring/branch carbons donates exactly one H (the CH, the CH3 and the CH2), and the three H's land one on each oxygen that ends up as an O-H in the drawn product -- the phosphoryl O becomes =O+H and the two ring oxygens become P-OH after their C-O bonds break; (b) the C3H3. neutral is encoded as the allenyl/propargyl radical CH2=C=CH. (one localized resonance form of the delocalized C3H3 radical, convention C) because that is what the chosen H-loss pattern produces; the book writes only the formula 'C3H3.' and does not draw its structure. ENCODING NOTE: none of the three migrating H's can be atom-mapped (RDKit folds a mapped explicit H into implicit valence, verified in the project container), so the five moves express the net heavy-atom bookkeeping of the eight underlying fishhooks: <1> the phosphoryl oxygen's odd electron pairs with the H arriving from the methyl carbon, and the electron that methyl carbon keeps becomes half of the new C6=C7 pi bond (compressed into one move O(2) -> bond(6,7)); <2> one electron of the C(6)-O(5) bond goes to O(5), which hands it to the H arriving from C(6), whose own leftover electron completes the C6=C7 pi bond (compressed into bond(5,6) -> bond(6,7)); <3> the other C(6)-O(5) electron and <4> one C(8)-O(9) electron form the new C6=C8 pi bond; <5> the second C(8)-O(9) electron goes to O(9) -> its O-H, while the electron C(8) keeps after losing its H stays as the radical (compressed into bond(8,9) -> atom(8)). NO PRINTED NUMBERS: Equation 8.80 shows no m/z and no abundance, so detected=false, peak status 'inferred' and no relative_intensity; m/z 112.9998 and precursor m/z 152.0233 are curator-computed monoisotopic values for the drawn structures, not book data.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.80, and no cross-link is asserted. This was checked, not assumed: (a) NO rule in the 154-rule index contains a phosphorus atom at all (regex over every DFS), and none is a triple-H transfer -- the largest multiple-H family is h2Transiton_1/2/3 ('2 H transition'), which moves only two hydrogens and requires the H-accepting core to be '[C]6([C]7){=}[_A+.]8', a CARBON bearing the ionized heteroatom, whereas here that atom is P; (b) empirically, the entire enabled fragmentation rule list was applied to the drawn molecular ion inside the project container (MOD DG.apply, Term/Specialisation) and only two placeholder rules matched at all ('Substituion §R1S2-3Y4' and 'inductive cleavage odd electron 1 4.18 §R1Y2'), neither of which produced a single concrete product -- every returned graph still carried unbound '_A' placeholders. So the MOD forward model currently has no channel for this reaction.
